tests.title: Unit 1: Introduction to Economics – Practice Test 1

questions.question_text: A critic argues that a definition of economics wrongly treats wealth as the end and human welfare as the means. Which definition is being criticised?
questions.explanation: The wealth definition made wealth the end; critics (Ruskin, Carlyle) said man was reduced to a means.

questions.question_text: Which pairing of economist and the main criticism of his definition is correct?
options: Robbins – confines economics to material welfare
Smith – ignores the role of production in a nation
Marshall – ignores scarcity and choice among alternative uses
questions.explanation: Marshall's welfare definition did not bring in scarcity and had the artificial material/non-material split.

questions.question_text: A teacher's tuition services give satisfaction but are not material goods. Which definition would have difficulty counting this as economic activity?
options: None; all of them exclude services
questions.explanation: Marshall limited economics to material welfare; services of teachers and doctors were treated as non-material.

questions.question_text: Which feature belongs to Robbins' definition but NOT to Marshall's?
options: Emphasis on wealth as a means to welfare
Focus on choice among scarce means with alternative uses
questions.explanation: Robbins stressed ends, scarce means, alternative uses and choice.

questions.question_text: If every want of every person could be met without using up any resource, which element of Robbins' definition would disappear?
questions.explanation: Scarcity of means gives rise to choice. Without it, there is no economic problem.

questions.question_text: "Economics is neutral between ends" means that an economist, as an economist, would:
options: Condemn goods whose production harms public health
Refuse to analyse markets in goods that are illegal
Study how scarce means are allocated, not judge the ends
Rank wants according to how morally worthy they are
questions.explanation: Robbins separated economics from ethics: it studies the allocation of means, not whether ends are good.

questions.question_text: Which dimension does Samuelson's definition add to earlier definitions?
options: The creation of wealth as the end of production
The material welfare of ordinary people in society
Growth over time, in money or barter economies
The pattern of income distribution among classes
questions.explanation: It covers choice over time ("now or in the future") and economies with or without money.

questions.question_text: A student says "scarcity and shortage mean the same". Which reply is correct?
options: Scarcity occurs only in poor countries; shortage occurs everywhere
Scarcity is a universal condition of limited resources; shortage is excess demand at a given price
Scarcity is a temporary gap at a given price; shortage is a permanent condition
Shortage comes from unlimited wants; scarcity comes from price controls
questions.explanation: Scarcity exists in every economy; a shortage is a market imbalance at a particular (often controlled) price.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a free good in the economic sense?
options: Drinking water supplied by a municipality
questions.explanation: A free good is available in unlimited supply with no opportunity cost; the others involve cost.

questions.question_text: Which characteristic of human wants explains why the demand for a good rises again after being satisfied?
questions.explanation: Recurrence: a want satisfied today returns (hunger returns).

questions.question_text: Which pair shows complementary wants?
questions.explanation: Complementary wants are satisfied together.

questions.question_text: The scope of economics covers its nature and its subject matter. Which of these is a question about its NATURE?
options: Whether economics is a science or an art and positive or normative
How the output of an economy is distributed among factors
How goods are exchanged in markets
questions.explanation: Nature concerns what kind of discipline it is; subject matter covers consumption, production, exchange and distribution.

questions.question_text: Which activity shows economics being applied as an ART?
options: Collecting income data for a national survey of households
A minister uses economic knowledge to design a subsidy
Observing that quantity demanded falls when price rises
Explaining the causes of an episode of inflation
questions.explanation: Art means using knowledge to achieve practical ends such as policy.

questions.question_text: Why are economic laws said to be "tendencies" rather than exact laws?
options: They apply only to the past
Human behaviour varies and conditions are not controlled
They use too many assumptions about mathematics
questions.explanation: Economic laws state what generally happens under given conditions.

questions.question_text: In a study of the effect of price on demand, a researcher holds income, tastes and related prices constant. This is the assumption of:
questions.explanation: Ceteris paribus isolates the effect of one variable.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a POSITIVE statement?
options: The government should raise the minimum wage soon
Income tax ought to be made more progressive
A higher minimum wage reduces jobs in small firms
Every citizen deserves access to free healthcare
questions.explanation: It states a cause-and-effect claim that can be tested against data (even if it may be false).

questions.question_text: A statement says "A 10% rise in petrol price reduced demand by 4%." Which classification is correct?
options: Positive only if it is true
Positive, because it can be checked with data
questions.explanation: Positive statements can be tested; truth is not required for classification.

questions.question_text: Which statement is NORMATIVE?
options: Subsidies on fuel ought to be removed
India's fiscal deficit was 5.6% of GDP
questions.explanation: "Ought" signals a value judgement.

questions.question_text: Which pairing of method and procedure is correct?
options: Inductive method: from general assumptions to particular cases
Deductive method: from particular facts to a general law
Deductive method: from general assumptions to specific conclusions
Inductive method: logic alone, without any observation
questions.explanation: Deduction starts with assumptions; induction starts with observation.

questions.question_text: An economist collects data on household savings for many years and derives a general pattern. She is using:
questions.explanation: Induction moves from observed particulars to a generalisation.

questions.question_text: Who coined the terms micro and macro economics?
questions.explanation: Frisch (1933).

questions.question_text: Which question belongs to MACROeconomics?
options: How does a farmer decide which crop mix to grow?
How does a firm decide the price of its soap?
Why did the price of onions rise in one city last month?
What explains a simultaneous fall in national output and employment?
questions.explanation: Total output and employment are economy-wide aggregates.

questions.question_text: The "paradox of thrift" is an illustration of:
questions.explanation: What is true for one individual (saving more) need not hold for everyone together.

questions.question_text: One farmer gains by selling more wheat. If all farmers sell more, prices may fall and total income may not rise. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: The whole behaves differently from the part.

questions.question_text: Partial equilibrium analysis differs from general equilibrium analysis in that partial equilibrium:
options: Examines only the market for consumer goods
Examines one market while other markets are held constant
Examines all markets and their interdependence together
questions.explanation: Marshall used partial analysis; Walras developed general equilibrium.

tests.title: Unit 1: Introduction to Economics – Practice Test 2

questions.question_text: The main limitation of macroeconomic analysis is that it:
options: Is concerned only with the determination of prices
Does not deal with questions of government policy
Cannot deal with the idea of national income
May hide differences among units behind aggregates
questions.explanation: Averages and totals can conceal very different experiences of households and sectors.

questions.question_text: "What, how and for whom to produce" are problems in every economy because:
options: Resources are unlimited but badly distributed
Governments restrict how resources can be used
Resources are limited relative to wants and alternative uses exist
Money is not available to all the producers
questions.explanation: Scarcity with alternative uses forces choice.

questions.question_text: The choice between labour-intensive and capital-intensive methods is a problem of:
questions.explanation: It is a choice of technique.

questions.question_text: A government decides to produce more defence goods and fewer consumer goods. Which problem is mainly involved?
questions.explanation: Choice of product mix and quantities.

questions.question_text: Which statement about "for whom to produce" is correct?
options: It is solved only in socialist economies
It depends on the pattern of income distribution
questions.explanation: Purchasing power determines who gets the goods.

questions.question_text: In which economy do prices primarily solve the basic problems?
questions.explanation: The price mechanism allocates resources through demand and supply.

questions.question_text: India is described as a mixed economy mainly because:
options: Public and private sectors co-exist under regulation
The government fixes the prices of every good sold
The state owns all the heavy industries in the country
Private ownership is allowed only inside agriculture
questions.explanation: Both sectors operate, with markets plus state regulation and planning.

questions.question_text: An allocation is Pareto efficient when:
options: No one can gain without another person losing
Total output of the economy is at its maximum
Income is shared equally among all the persons
Price equals average cost for every single firm
questions.explanation: It describes a position where any change helps one person only at another's expense.

questions.question_text: Allocative efficiency is achieved where:
questions.explanation: Resources are allocated to goods in the combination society values most.

questions.question_text: Productive efficiency is achieved when:
options: Goods are produced at the lowest possible cost on the PPC
All resources are fully employed in any use
Output is the combination consumers value most
Income is distributed fairly among workers
questions.explanation: Resources are used so that cost per unit is minimised; allocative efficiency concerns the mix produced.

questions.question_text: The opportunity cost of attending a Rs 1,00,000 course for a student who could have earned Rs 2,00,000 working that year is best measured as:
questions.explanation: Fees plus the earnings forgone.

questions.question_text: Which statement is TRUE about opportunity cost?
options: It is always measured in money
It equals the money cost of the choice
It is the value of the best alternative forgone
It applies only to scarce goods in market economies
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the next-best alternative given up.

questions.question_text: A farmer can produce either 300 quintals of wheat or 450 quintals of rice. The opportunity cost of 1 quintal of rice is:
questions.explanation: 300/450 wheat per quintal of rice.

questions.question_text: If the opportunity cost of producing a good is zero, the good is:
questions.explanation: No alternative is forgone.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT an assumption behind the usual PPC?
options: Resources are equally efficient in producing both goods
Resources are fully and efficiently employed
questions.explanation: The usual PPC assumes resources are not equally suited to both goods, which gives its concave shape.

questions.question_text: The PPC is concave to the origin mainly because of:
questions.explanation: Shifting resources to less suitable uses raises the cost.

questions.question_text: If the PPC is a straight line, the marginal rate of transformation is:
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is constant when resources are equally suited.

questions.question_text: On an economy's PPC for guns and butter, moving from point A (10 guns, 40 butter) to B (12 guns, 30 butter) shows that the opportunity cost of 1 gun is:
questions.explanation: 2 guns cost 10 butter, so 5 butter per gun.

questions.question_text: Moving from B (12 guns, 30 butter) to C (14 guns, 15 butter) shows the opportunity cost of a gun has:
questions.explanation: 15 butter for 2 guns = 7.5 per gun, up from 5.

questions.question_text: An economy operating at a point inside its PPC indicates:
options: Output that cannot be reached with present resources
Unemployment or inefficient use of resources
questions.explanation: The point is attainable but wasteful.

questions.question_text: The discovery of new oil reserves would cause the PPC for oil and other goods to:
questions.explanation: More resources increase capacity.

questions.question_text: A technological improvement in the production of only wheat will cause the PPC to:
options: Pivot outward along the wheat axis
Pivot outward along the other axis
questions.explanation: Only the wheat intercept rises.

questions.question_text: A severe flood destroys part of a country's capital stock. The PPC:
questions.explanation: Productive capacity falls.

questions.question_text: A move from a point inside the PPC to a point on it indicates:
questions.explanation: Better use of existing resources; the curve itself has not moved.

questions.question_text: The distinction between movement along a PPC and a shift of the PPC is that a shift shows:
questions.explanation: Movement is reallocation; shift is growth or decline.

tests.title: Unit 1: Introduction to Economics – Practice Test 3

questions.question_text: On a PPC, producing more of one good means producing less of the other because:
options: Prices of the two goods are fixed by the government
Wants for the two goods are limited
Resources are limited and can be used in alternative ways
questions.explanation: Scarcity with alternative uses creates a trade-off.

questions.question_text: Which event would NOT shift the PPC?
questions.explanation: Reducing unemployment moves the economy to the frontier.

questions.question_text: A country's PPC bows inward (convex) only if:
questions.explanation: Convex shape means falling marginal opportunity cost; it is rare.

questions.question_text: The marginal rate of transformation at a point on the PPC is equal to:
options: The slope of the PPC at that point
questions.explanation: MRT = −ΔY/ΔX along the curve.

questions.question_text: Which of the following shows the "problem of full employment" rather than the "problem of allocation"?
options: An economy operating inside its PPC
questions.explanation: It is a question of idle resources.

questions.question_text: "Economic growth" can be represented on the PPC diagram by:
options: An outward shift of the curve
questions.explanation: More capacity over time.

questions.question_text: Which is a reason to study economics beyond solving personal problems?
options: It removes scarcity from the entire economy
It guarantees steady profits for every firm
It permanently eliminates unemployment in the economy
It helps governments design fiscal and monetary policy
questions.explanation: Policy design requires economic analysis.

questions.question_text: Which of these would an economist classify as a factor of production?
options: A government permit to run a manufacturing unit
A bank loan taken out by a business firm
Cash that is kept in the hand of the owner
The organisation and risk-bearing of an entrepreneur
questions.explanation: The four factors are land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship.

questions.question_text: Reward for the factor "capital" is:
questions.explanation: Land: rent; labour: wages; entrepreneur: profit.

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly distinguishes normative from positive statements?
options: Positive statements say what ought to be done
Positive statements cannot be checked against evidence
Normative statements rest on value judgements that data alone cannot settle
Normative statements are always false and positive ones always true
questions.explanation: Facts can test positive claims; values cannot be settled by facts alone.

questions.question_text: Two economists agree on the facts about the effects of a tax but disagree on whether it should be imposed. Their disagreement is mainly:
questions.explanation: They differ in values.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of a macroeconomic variable?
questions.explanation: It is an aggregate.

questions.question_text: "The price of wheat will fall if its supply rises, other things being equal" is:
options: A normative statement about agricultural policy
An ethical judgement about the welfare of farmers
A statement of settled historical fact only
A positive statement using ceteris paribus
questions.explanation: It is testable and isolates one cause.

questions.question_text: The deductive method is most useful when an economist wants to:
options: Summarise the historical records of an economy
Collect and tabulate raw data from field surveys
Conduct a controlled experiment in a laboratory setting
Derive logical implications from assumptions for later testing
questions.explanation: Theory is built from assumptions by logic.

questions.question_text: The inductive method is most useful for:
options: Arriving at general patterns from observed data
Building a logical model from assumptions
questions.explanation: It moves from observation to generalisation.

questions.question_text: Which example best illustrates the fallacy of composition?
options: Different consumers buy very different bundles of goods
Prices rise when the supply of money expands
A rise in the price of a good reduces its demand
One spectator who stands sees better, but if all stand nobody does
questions.explanation: What is true for a part is not necessarily true for the whole.

questions.question_text: Which statement about microeconomics is correct?
options: It is also called price theory
It is also called income and employment theory
questions.explanation: Micro explains price determination.

questions.question_text: Keynes's General Theory (1936) is associated with:
questions.explanation: It founded modern macroeconomics.

questions.question_text: Why would a management student benefit from studying economics?
options: It removes all the risk from business decisions
It predicts movements in share prices exactly
It eliminates competition among the firms of an industry
It explains markets, costs, demand and policy settings
questions.explanation: Business decisions depend on economic conditions.

questions.question_text: A person gives up a job paying Rs 40,000 a month to run her own shop and earns Rs 30,000 profit a month. Her economic profit is:
questions.explanation: Economic profit subtracts the implicit cost (forgone salary).

questions.question_text: A country moves from a command economy to a market economy. Which central problem is now primarily solved through prices instead of planning?
options: What, how and for whom to produce
questions.explanation: The price mechanism guides all three allocation problems.

questions.question_text: The economic problem faced by an individual consumer is best described as:
options: Having no source of income of any kind
Being unable to find suitable employment anywhere
Having to pay taxes on income to the government
Choosing among alternatives with limited income and time
questions.explanation: Limited means with alternative uses require choice.

questions.question_text: A household spends Rs 5,000 on a phone instead of a family trip. This decision illustrates:
questions.explanation: The trip is the next-best alternative given up.

questions.question_text: A firm owns a building that it could rent out for Rs 8 lakh a year, and uses it as its own office. The annual implicit cost of using the building is:
options: Zero, as no rent is paid
Equal to the building's purchase price
questions.explanation: Implicit cost is the value of the best alternative use of a self-owned resource.

questions.question_text: Which of the following would be a normative question about the Indian economy?
options: Should the government subsidise higher education?
How many people are below the poverty line?
By how much did GDP grow last year?
questions.explanation: "Should" indicates a value judgement.

tests.title: Unit 1: Introduction to Economics – Practice Test 4

questions.question_text: The Greek word "oikonomia" suggests that economics was first viewed as:
options: A law of value and price
questions.explanation: Oikos means household and nomos means management.

questions.question_text: Which criticism is made of Robbins' scarcity definition?
options: It confines economics to the study of wealth only
It is restricted to the material welfare of people
It overlooks growth and welfare and is purely positive
It ignores the very problem of scarcity itself
questions.explanation: Critics said it neglects growth, welfare and normative aspects.

questions.question_text: Which of these is a genuine limitation of macroeconomics?
options: It is concerned only with the study of prices of goods
It is a branch of ethics and not of economics
It may ignore structure and differences inside the economy
It cannot be used to study aggregate demand at all
questions.explanation: Aggregation hides structural differences.

questions.question_text: An economy has idle factories and unemployed workers. This implies that:
questions.explanation: Resources are not fully used.

questions.question_text: If an economy shifts resources from consumer goods to capital goods, in the long run the PPC is likely to:
questions.explanation: More capital raises future capacity.

questions.question_text: Why does the opportunity cost of producing more of a good rise as the economy shifts resources toward it?
options: Resources are specialised and not equally suited to both
The prices of all goods in the economy are rising
The marginal utility of that good keeps diminishing
Human wants for the good are unlimited in nature
questions.explanation: Less suitable resources must be moved, so more of the other good is lost per extra unit.

questions.question_text: Which statement is NOT correct about the scope of economics?
options: It covers consumption, production, exchange and distribution
It is both positive and normative in parts
It is concerned with choices under scarcity
questions.explanation: Public policy is part of economics.

questions.question_text: Compared with sociology, economics mainly analyses:
options: The choice and allocation of scarce resources
The behaviour of social groups only
The cultural values of a community
The customs and norms of society
questions.explanation: Its focus is choice under scarcity.

questions.question_text: Which pair correctly matches a branch of economics and an example?
options: Microeconomics – inflation rate in an economy
questions.explanation: Aggregates are macro.

questions.question_text: "The rich should pay more tax" is a normative statement because it:
options: Refers to a government revenue source
Can be proved or disproved with data
Expresses a value judgement about fairness
questions.explanation: "Should" reflects a value, not a testable fact.

questions.question_text: An economy can produce 100 units of X and 0 of Y, or 0 of X and 50 of Y, with constant opportunity cost. The opportunity cost of 1 unit of Y is:
questions.explanation: 100/50 = 2 units of X per unit of Y.

questions.question_text: For the same economy, producing 40 units of X means the maximum of Y is:
questions.explanation: X = 40 uses 40% of capacity, leaving 60% for Y: 0.6 × 50 = 30.

questions.question_text: A combination of 60 X and 30 Y for the same economy (PPC: 100 X or 50 Y, straight line) is:
questions.explanation: 60/100 + 30/50 = 1.2, which is more than 1, so it is beyond the frontier and unattainable.

questions.question_text: Which of the following will NOT change the shape of a PPC?
questions.explanation: Unemployment moves the point inside the curve; the curve itself stays.

questions.question_text: Which topic is studied under public finance, part of the scope of economics?
options: Pricing of a single firm's product in a market
Consumer preference between two brands of tea
The household budget of a family on income
How governments raise and spend money
questions.explanation: Public finance studies taxation, public expenditure and public debt.

questions.question_text: The PPC illustrates opportunity cost because it shows that:
options: The price levels of the two goods are different
More of one good means giving up some of the other
Consumer incomes are unequally distributed in society
Profit rises as the total output of goods rises
questions.explanation: The slope represents the sacrifice.

questions.question_text: An increase in the number of skilled workers will most likely:
questions.explanation: Capacity rises.

questions.question_text: Using a plot of land for housing instead of farming involves:
options: A sunk cost that was incurred for earlier crops
The opportunity cost of crops forgone
No cost, because the land is already owned
Only the money cost of putting up a building
questions.explanation: The best alternative use is given up.

questions.question_text: Which statement about the PPC is correct?
options: Points inside the curve show efficient production
The curve must always be a straight line
Points outside the curve can be reached with present resources
Every point on the curve shows efficient use of resources
questions.explanation: Points on the frontier mean full employment with the best technology.

questions.question_text: The statement "A fall in the price of tea increases demand for tea, other things being equal" is:
questions.explanation: It is a testable cause-effect claim.

questions.question_text: A student cannot decide whether a statement is positive or normative. The most useful test is whether it:
options: Could in principle be checked against data
Concerns the policies of the government
Is expressed in one long and detailed sentence
questions.explanation: Positive statements are testable; normative ones express values.

questions.question_text: On a PPC, long-run economic growth requires:
options: Additions to capacity through saving and investment
A rise in the general level of prices
A movement along the existing curve
A fall in the rate of unemployment only
questions.explanation: Growth shifts the frontier outward.

questions.question_text: The four traditional divisions of economics are:
questions.explanation: They describe the subject matter.

questions.question_text: In which situation is the opportunity cost of using a machine for production lowest?
options: When the machine has no alternative use
When the machine has many alternative profitable uses
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost depends on the next-best use; with none, it is zero.

questions.question_text: The basic economic problem is the same for a rich and a poor country because:
options: Wants exceed available resources in both
questions.explanation: Scarcity is universal; only the extent differs.
